A Shared Causal Platform
  for a Universal Bank
Sponsor proposal and construction decision


         Research and product proposal

                7 October 2026
                  Version 2.0
The proposed investment

Build a common scientific library and an independent workbench for bank policy and time-
series analysis, repeated decisions under partial observation, and temporal causal discovery
with automatic data organization. The product should preserve what was known at each
decision, what intervention is being compared, what identifies its effect, and which financial
outcome it changes. Other applications can use the same operations through an SDK and
evidence exports.
   The recommended first commitment is a six-month construction and bank-design tranche,
illustratively USD 1.14 million plus bank-owner, independent-validation and security partici-
pation still to be priced. All three scientific workspaces start in this tranche. Their release
claims differ: a qualified policy effect, a conditional latent-model scenario and an ambiguous
causal graph are useful but distinct outputs. The team should implement a narrow supported
path in each workspace and measure whether their common foundation actually saves work.
   A large shared product is not automatically the least expensive choice. Under the proposal’s
explicit equal-output assumptions, workflow savings alone require roughly 27 completed
equivalent studies annually. Low reuse and delayed adoption favor a capable team composing
existing tools. Further investment should depend on measured reuse or additional decision
value, with that expert team as the comparator.


The banking problem
A promotion can raise deposit balances while reducing funding contribution because the higher
rate reprices the existing book. A collections action can change next month’s eligibility and the
distribution of future arrears. A regression on loan growth can confuse borrower demand with
bank supply. A predictive hidden-state model can fit historical observations while misvaluing a
new policy if staff used private information when taking actions. These are different economic
questions requiring different designs.
   Banking literature provides concrete precedents: local deposit-market structure and monetary
transmission (Drechsler et al., 2017); comparisons of differently affected banks lending to the
same firm (Mian and Khwaja, 2006); refinancing eligibility distinguished from self-selected take-
up (Agarwal et al., 2020); and demand/supply models for market-wide mortgage regulation
(Benetton, 2021). Their coefficients are not ready-made estimates for a new bank campaign.
Their designs explain which variation, measurements and assumptions a product must preserve.


What the product delivers
The policy and transmission workspace evaluates customer interventions, staggered branch
changes, bank-firm supply shocks and dynamic response paths. It preserves comparison groups,
target weights, common economic shocks and financial covariance. The sequential workspace

                                               2
                                                                                                3


compares explicit strategies, fits controlled latent-state models and carries action selection
and observation uncertainty into conditional policy values. The discovery and data workspace
reconstructs historical information, proposes semantic mappings, preserves uncertain entity
links and investigates graph structure under declared restrictions.
   An analyst moves from a bank decision to a reconstructible study. A product owner receives
contribution, customer outcomes, uncertainty and unresolved conditions. A reviewer can
inspect the original account and estimator. A developer consumes the same typed result rather
than reinterpreting an unlabeled effect array. The proposed standalone application deploys
within the institution’s controlled environment; no named banking group is an existing client
or endorser of this proposal.
   The common library should build temporal semantics, study orchestration, financial recon-
ciliation, score/inference contracts and evidence export. It should reuse established estimators
and planning/discovery engines. The survey covers 44 open-source projects, with preserved
license and documentation observations. Examples include DoWhy, DoubleML/EconML,
panel and R longitudinal methods, Tigramite and POMDP/state-space ecosystems (py-why
contributors, 2026a; DoubleML contributors, 2026; py-why contributors, 2026b; bcallaway11
contributors, 2026; nt-williams contributors, 2026; jakobrunge contributors, 2026; probml
contributors, 2026; JuliaPOMDP contributors, 2026). These are source assessments; they are
not claims that all packages have been runtime-qualified together.


What has actually been constructed
The research package includes a technical monograph, 87 scholarly PDFs, three official guidance
PDFs, traceable sources and material claims, fitted synthetic banking studies and four JSON
contracts. Two narrow Python components implement historical event-revision selection and
mergeable crossed-cluster score reduction. The full compiler, service, workspaces and sibling
adapters remain a proposed product.
  The studies go beyond favorable demonstrations. A 96-branch deposit rollout has positive
balance effects but estimated monthly contribution near negative USD 5,219 per treated branch.
The collections study compares direct, importance-weighted and doubly robust policy estimates;
a plausible current-action weighting shortcut values the wrong sustained policy. Repeated
samples retain nominal-interval coverage failures.
   An unknown-emission hidden-state study estimates initial probabilities, transitions and
observations from signals/actions alone. On observational data, omitting hidden action
selection reverses the model’s policy-gain sign; a longer convergence check preserves the failure.
Modeling that selection improves the stated experiment but leaves substantial policy-value
uncertainty. It does not establish generic observational identification.
   The bank-firm example separates supply from demand through borrower effects. A 1,200-
panel experiment shows how common shocks invalidate row-independent uncertainty. Two
structural timing assumptions generate different impulse responses with the same observed
Gaussian VAR law. Exact short-path checks independently verify selected likelihood and
sequential-score identities. All are synthetic research evidence, not measured bank uplift.
   The ten-million-row component measurement takes about 1.2 seconds and 123 MiB peak
resident memory in this environment. It generates and reduces precomputed two-dimensional
scores. It excludes source reads, temporal reconstruction, nuisance fitting, POMDP fitting
and graph search. It supports a component construction choice, not an enterprise-scale service
promise.
Cost, execution and acceptance

A fair construction comparator

Both alternatives must deliver the same completed studies: a frozen population, credible
identifying design, suitable reference comparison, economic account and reconstructible review
evidence. Expert composition uses more study-specific code; the shared product automates
recurring work. The cost model does not give the expert team weaker scientific obligations.
  The illustrative three-year comparison uses a 10% discount rate. Expert composition has
USD 1 million initial shared work, USD 0.6 million annual common operation and USD 150,000
per completed study. The product has USD 4 million initial work, USD 1.8 million annual
operation and USD 60,000 per study. These are assumptions, not quotes or measured savings.
The USD 1.14 million first tranche is included within the product build.


                  Scenario         Expert cost Platform cost Platform saving
                  Low reuse             5.476         9.670           -4.194
                  Moderate reuse       11.445        12.057           -0.613
                  High reuse           15.921        13.848            2.073
                  Adoption ramp         8.402        10.840           -2.438


Amounts are present costs in USD millions. The first three scenarios have 8, 24 and 36 studies
every year; the ramp has 4, 16 and 30. A positive saving favors the product. The 24-study
case needs approximately USD 246,000 additional constant annual decision benefit to cover its
cost premium. The ramp needs about USD 980,000. Only value beyond what the expert team
would achieve belongs in this account.
   The assumed USD 90,000 saving per study equals 3.6 person-months at the planning staffing
rate. That needs evidence. If the saving halves, the cost-only reuse threshold doubles to
roughly 53 studies annually. Customer and country-specific semantic work, validation and
support may substantially reduce reuse. Count failed studies and outcome-maturity delays
in both alternatives. Do not add analyst savings twice or treat synthetic policy gains as
commercial revenue.


The first six months

Staff one product/economics lead, two causal/econometric scientists, two data/platform
engineers and one application engineer. At an assumed USD 25,000 loaded person-month, 36
person-months cost USD 900,000. Adding USD 50,000 compute/tooling and 20% contingency
gives the USD 1.14 million illustrative tranche. The bank-specific estimate must also price
business/data owners, independent validation and security.

                                                4
                                                                                              5


   In the first month, select a funding rollout, a repeated-decision history and a temporal
mechanism question. Inspect action logs, historical availability, ownership and outcome
maturity. Agree the equivalent-work baseline and required evidence. During months two and
three, construct the common snapshot/evidence path, qualify a limited panel/longitudinal path,
and implement finite-state estimation and a temporal graph adapter with explicit scientific
status.
   During months four through six, complete bounded workspaces and have a second analyst
reconstruct their studies. Compare active analyst/reviewer hours, calendar delay, unresolved
material findings and economic relevance with expert composition. A proposed 30% effort
reduction is a target to test. Bank-scale storage, full estimator training and retry behavior
require separate workload qualification; a fast arithmetic kernel does not satisfy it.
   Subsequent tranches expand supported histories, measurement models, discovery assump-
tions, distributed execution and independent-product support only when the scientific and
cost evidence warrants them. The roadmap does not postpone POMDP/discovery work to
an undefined later product, nor promise that all three workspaces can authorize operational
customer policies in six months.


Reuse across the existing repositories
FinMarketing can export assignment episodes and group contribution components, then con-
sume policy effects with their target and covariance. dataml can supply masks, recovery
assumptions and uncertainty draws. BayesFilter can supply numerical filtering/estimation
components while the causal library owns the action model and intervention interpretation.
MacroFinance can exchange shock restrictions and response paths; cardnpv requires explicit
contrast-sign conversion. These are proposed integrations based on inspected local documenta-
tion (Workspace project contributors, 2026), with concrete acceptance journeys in the technical
monograph. No sibling repository was changed by this work.


What would stop or narrow the investment
Narrow the target when action support or data coverage is inadequate. Return conditional
scenarios or bounds when historical policy value is unidentified. Keep graph ambiguity visible.
Stop a statistical release when numerical stability or relevant interval calibration fails. Stop
common platform expansion if most applications require bespoke work and the measured
savings do not cover shared cost. Useful data and study components can survive a negative
result for another module.
  For deployment, the bank needs actual access authorization, independent model validation,
operational ownership and qualified dependencies. The April 2026 US guidance supersedes
SR11-7 and SR21-8 and has specified scope, including an exclusion for generative/agentic
models (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and other federal banking agencies,
2026). PRA SS1/23 has a revised April 2026 version with specified institutional applicability
(Bank of England Prudential Regulation Authority, 2026). The product supplies evidence for
the applicable review process; the proposal does not confer approval.
